title: Jetrun tiles
description: Every tile a page of the world can hold, keyed by the tile's name, in the form Cyberun's landscape renderer reads (ADR 0007): a list of pieces, straight runs of identical steps, given as Cyberun's tile records give them. Pages are 224 pixels across and 160 down; a piece may run on into the next page. See examples/jetrun/GLOSSARY.md and world.py.

upsideDown.description: Drawn upside down, Cyberun's $99 marker: floors become ceilings, a flat piece's y is XORed with 12, a wall moves 8 pixels.

mirrored.description: Drawn mirrored left to right, Cyberun's $FF marker. A flat run ending on the page's edge (end code 22) is left where it is.

x.description: The piece's start, its lowest point, in Cyberun's page coordinates: 8 is the page's left edge. For a piece climbing left, the left edge of its lowest step; for a rock-left wall, the byte left of its edge.

y.description: The bottom line of the piece's lowest step, in Cyberun's page coordinates: 24 is the page's top line.

direction.description: The steps' shape: Cyberun's sixteen. Flat steps are 24 pixels long; gentle slopes 16 across and 8 up, plain ones 8 and 8, steep ones 8 and 16; walls 16 high. Floors have rock below, ceilings rock above; 'up' climbs to the right, 'down' climbs to the left.

ends.description: Flat pieces only: Cyberun's end codes for the run's first and last steps, which pick the caps it draws there. 0 none; 16 and 17 a left end, 18 and 19 a right end, the odd ones where the end is a drop; 22 ($16) only the first column of the last step, which ends a run on the page's right edge.
